rounds.text: Aurum Proptech Ltd is demonstrating an undeniable acceleration in top-line growth, with compounded sales surging by 109% over 5 years, 44% over 3 years, and 65% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16, E17]. This strong operational momentum is translating directly to profitability, highlighted by compounded profit growth reaching 103% over the trailing twelve months alongside a rules-based screen scoring a high 88 out of 100 with a medium-confidence BUY signal [E19, E63]. Operating margins have also expanded dramatically to 25% in the TTM from just 1% three years prior, while generating real cash with ₹63 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹47 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E28, E33, E34]. Furthermore, capital expenditure phase-outs are evident as capital work-in-progress (CWIP) dropped by 41.7% to ₹7 Cr, signaling that new capacity is coming online [E39]. Market recognition is starting to build, backed by a strong relative-strength rating of 89 against the Nifty 500 and a reverse DCF indicating that the current price requires a modest 13.2% growth rate to justify its valuation [E45, E49]. Conceded: [E9] and [E10], which show low or negative return metrics such as an ROE of -2.06% and ROCE of 1.63% lagging sector benchmarks.

Aurum Proptech Ltd trades at an exorbitant price-to-earnings ratio of 1714x [E1], while its return on equity sits deeply in negative territory at -2.06% against a sector benchmark of 10.41% [E9], and its median return on equity over the last 3 and 5 years has languished at -12% [E25, E26]. The fundamental earning power of the business is further compromised by a low return on capital employed of just 1.3% [E12] and a low interest coverage ratio [E59]. Moreover, earnings quality is highly suspect because they include a massive other income component of Rs. 86.4 Cr [E62], masking underlying operational weakness. Compounded sales growth over a 10-year horizon is -7% [E14], and compounded share price growth over the same decade is -4% [E20], underscoring a long-term pattern of stagnation. Promoter confidence is clearly waning, evidenced by promoters slashing their stake from 50.34% in Dec 2023 to 38.09% by Sep 2026 [E40]. Finally, the stock carries extreme downside risk characterized by an annualized volatility of 56.3% [E52] and a horrifying historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -76.1% [E51]. conceded: [E15]

The bear attacks the high P/E of 1714x [E1], but this metric ignores the immense operational inflection underway where trailing twelve month compounded sales growth has surged by 65% [E17] and three-year sales growth is 44% [E16], proving that top-line momentum is accelerating rapidly. While historical ROE has been negative [E25, E26], the bear overlooks the dramatic structural turnaround in operating margins, which expanded by 24 percentage points to 25% in the TTM period [E28] and further hit 26% in the June quarter [E29], driving a 103% surge in TTM profit growth [E19]. The long-term ten-year sales decline cited by the bear [E14] is completely outdated and eclipsed by the recent 5-year compounded sales growth of 109% [E15], demonstrating that the business has successfully scaled out of its historical stagnation. Furthermore, the concern over capital efficiency is answered by tangible financial strength: the company generated Rs 63 Cr in operating cash flow [E33] and Rs 47 Cr in free cash flow [E34] as capital expenditure winds down with CWIP dropping 41.7% [E39], indicating that cash generation is robust. Regarding promoter holding, the bear ignores that foreign institutional investors have stepped in to initiate and increase their stake [E41], while the rules-based screen independently awards the stock a strong 88 out of 100 BUY rating driven by exceptional YoY sales and profit acceleration [E63, E64, E66]. conceded: [E1, E40, E52, E52]

conceded: [E17]. The bull's reliance on a 65% TTM sales surge ignores the reality of a staggering 1714x P/E ratio that prices in perfection without safety [E1, E70]. While the bull points to expanding operating margins reaching 25% and 26% [E28, E29], it glosses over the fact that current earnings are artificially propped up by Rs. 86.4 Cr of other income rather than core operations [E62]. The bull dismisses negative return on metrics, yet historical reality shows a 10-year median ROE of -1% and a persistent 3-year median ROE of -12% alongside a low current ROCE of 1.3% [E12, E24, E26]. Furthermore, the bull claims strong cash generation, but borrowings actually ticked up to Rs 225 Cr alongside a low interest coverage ratio [E38, E59]. Finally, the bull brushes off insider selling while promoters have slashed their stake from 50.34% down to 38.09% [E40].
